source.title: The Fabaceae in Northeastern Mexico (Subfamily Papilionoideae, Tribes Amorpheae, Brongniartieae, and Dalbergieae)

provenance_note: New research record; preserves preexisting source extracts, species JSON, photographic files, licenses and attribution; no learner scoring or public site changes.
gap_addressed: Prior horticultural source calls it trailing herbaceous groundcover with purple flowers; technical 2025 treatment describes a silvery-villous low scrambling subshrub with bicolored pea flowers.

morphology_directly_reported.habit: Small scandent subshrub; branches arch, then root upon touching the ground, forming colonies up to approximately 1 m across
morphology_directly_reported.flower_spikes: Compact, globose to elongated-cylindrical, generally 0.5–3 cm long
morphology_directly_reported.corolla: Bicolored; banner begins pale yellow or cream and reddens with age; wings and keel pink or purple

differentiation.Dalea_gypsophila: Similar rooting behavior but D. gypsophila has white papillae on leaflets; D. greggii has silvery-villous pubescence and lacks those white papillae.
differentiation.Dalea_frutescens: D. frutescens may occasionally root at stem tips but has glabrous rather than silvery-villous branch surfaces.

reconciliation: Not a reliable species-level contradiction: horticultural 'purple flowers' describes the visual impression, whereas the technical treatment separates banner versus wing/keel colors. 'Trailing groundcover' is horticultural habit; 'subshrub' describes woody character. Preserve both attributions; prefer source-specified individual petal colors in diagnostic material.
unresolved: No specimen/photo-level test performed; do not relabel current photos by petal color without viewing actual image
No county-level evaluation or BONAP range determination
integration_flag: Future learner should teach spreading silvery rooting stems and bicolored flowers, not purple-only absolute rule
